title: Antitrust Barriers to AI Safety Coordination
bottleneck: Frontier labs cannot legally coordinate on slowing capability races or standardizing safety practices without risking antitrust liability, even when coordination would serve public safety. Amodei's pacing proposal explicitly required a narrow government waiver for safety conversations — a waiver that does not exist. Safety-motivated coordination among labs looks legally identical to collusion, chilling even benign cooperation.
why_it_blocks: Competition law, designed for price-fixing, inadvertently blocks the safety coordination it was never meant to prevent. Even informal safety discussions among labs carry legal risk under current law.
current_state: No antitrust safe harbor for AI safety coordination has been enacted in the US or EU; the legal barrier stands. A legislative safe harbor would be straightforward to draft but has no political champion.
